TRADITIONS / METHODS / WORDS
Each tradition.
Its own vocabulary.
Historical approaches, calendrical systems and chart calculations have separate entries. The complete glossary keeps their names and definitions available.

  

    
CHARTS & FIELD NOTES
Western astrology
Classical, Hellenistic, medieval and modern approaches belong within their own historical contexts. The natal calculator uses an explicit zodiac, house system and reference frame.
Prepare a natal chart ↗Hellenistic astrology ↗Horoscope field note ↗

    
CHARTS & FIELD NOTES
Jyotisha · Indian astrology
Rāśi / D1 is the principal sign chart. Vargas are divisional calculations. Nakshatra, daśā, pañcāṅga and muhūrta retain their own definitions. North and South Indian diagrams are presentation formats.
Prepare a Jyotisha chart ↗Jyotisha vocabulary ↗

    
FIELD NOTES
Chinese astrology
BaZi / Four Pillars and Zi Wei Dou Shu have distinct chart structures and terminology. Their entries identify each system separately.
BaZi / Four Pillars ↗Zi Wei Dou Shu ↗

    
FIELD NOTES
Maya calendars
Tzolk’in, Haab’ and the Long Count retain their own calendrical definitions. The planetary horoscope described by AstroApp has its own method and a separate glossary entry.
Tzolk’in ↗Haab’ ↗Long Count ↗Planetary horoscope ↗

    
FIELD NOTES
Nahua calendars
Tonalpohualli is recorded under its Nahua name and context. Its vocabulary has a separate entry alongside the other calendrical traditions.
Tonalpohualli ↗

    
CULTURAL ATLAS
Diné / Navajo sky traditions
The cultural atlas gives community-specific sky knowledge and narratives their own context, names and sources.
Diné field notes & sources ↗

    
CONTEMPORARY SYSTEMS
Dreamspell
A contemporary calendar system, with its own glossary entry and terminology. Its method is identified separately from historical Maya counts.
Dreamspell definition ↗

    
HISTORICAL FIELD NOTES
Mesopotamian sky traditions
Babylonian celestial omens and later horoscopic practice retain their historical names and context in the lexicon.
Babylonian astrology ↗

  




A PLURAL APPROACH
Traditions in context.
Compare sources, language and practice while retaining the distinctions between traditions. No religious affiliation is required to explore the material.
FIELD NOTES
Room for doubt.
Record the chart or observation before its interpretation. Astrology is approached here as a cultural and symbolic practice, rather than an established scientific forecasting method.
